description: Installation of Smart Hub Unit with integrated digital screens
decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; white-space-collapse: preserve;">The proposed development, by virtue of its size, scale, detailed design, positioning, and method of illumination that includes sequential moving images, is visually intrusive and out of keeping with the local area. Because of the existing amount of street furniture on this stretch of pavement, it would </span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt; white-space: pre-wrap;">result in an unsightly proliferation of clutter within the street scene, and t</span><span style="background-color: transparent; font-size: 11pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; white-space: pre-wrap;">he harm caused to the wider conservation area is not outweighed by the minimal public benefit. As such, the proposal fails to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the </span><span style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif; white-space-collapse: preserve;">Clapton Pond Conservation Area and is contrary to policies D3 (Optimising site capacity through the design-led apprpach), D4 (Delivering good design), D8 (Public realm) and HC1 (Heritage Conservation and Growth) of the London Plan (2021) and policies PP1 (Public realm), LP1 (Design Quality and Local Character), LP3 (Designated Heritage Assets) and LP7 (Advertisements) of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020) and the Commercial Extensions and Alterations SPD (2026).</span></p>
